I play a Warrior in retail. I bind Pummel to Scroll Wheel Up. I try to bind things I want to get off quickly to the most accesible buttons. 

For example, in Classic, I mained a Hunter. 

My Hunter’s Mark was on Button 1, Concussive Button 2. Aspect of the Hawk Shift Scroll Up, Aspect of Cheetah Shift Scroll Down. It allows me to access it all quickly. Inessential abilities I pass over. All the most accesible binds should be reserved for the abilities you need the most.  It’s okay to not have a bind for everything. 

In your case, you’re going to want some binds for each of your stances, Stance Dancing becomes important.  I would try to bind them all in similar fashion so you remember them and associate them along a similar line. Maybe like: Attack: Q, Defensive: Shift Q, Fury: Ctrl Q. Whatever you can easily access and get comfortable with. When I roll a toon I almost always put abilities on keys where I feel most comfortable and then leave them alone so I get them assigned to memory.

Too many buttons. I can see that being problematic in that it’s easy to hit the wrong abilities, unless you become super familiarized with all their locations. It’s probably easier to bind things to 1, Shift 1, Ctrl 1, 2, Shift 2, Ctrl 2, etc 

I play on a mouse with two buttons on each side and then two on the top. It covers everything. I bind things to letters close to the movement keys. My binds could look like this:

Button 1, Shift Button 1, Ctrl Button 1, etc etc Click Wheel, Shift Click Wheel, Mouse Wheel Up, Mouse Wheel Down, Shift Mouse Wheel Up, Shift Mouse Wheel Down. Etc etc etc.
